claim: A column of soft grey-blue smoke with in-shader volume: layered domain-warped fbm rises and curls with depth-faded internal contrast — a smooth rising plume, no slab seams.

q1_defects.answer: Round-2 re-fix resolved the round-1 defect: the hard axis-aligned brick/shelf tile seams are GONE. Across idle and all three play frames the structure is organic curling swirls with soft billowing edges — no horizontal shelves, no rectangular masonry grid. bandingScore 0.228-0.243 is the over-report on organic noise detail the caveat warns about (down from round-1's 0.32-0.34), not real banding; visual inspection confirms no hard seams. Backend=webgpu, consoleErrors=[], networkErrors=[]. Only cosmetic note: the plume's lower edge is a fairly straight soft horizon, which is a frame boundary, not a tile seam.
evidence: metrics: idle bandingScore=0.239, play-2 bandingScore=0.233 (organic-noise over-report per caveat); consoleErrors=[] networkErrors=[]

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes — it now clearly reads as a soft rising smoke volume: layered grey plumes with curling internal contrast and depth-faded darker pockets, dense at the base and feathering upward. It no longer reads as the round-1 muddy warm-grey brick stack. The body is a low-saturation near-neutral grey (effHue~51, effSat 0.12) with a faint warm/cream cast rather than the claimed 'grey-blue'; per the caveat this warm-vs-cool tint is a taste FLAG, not a MUST-FIX, because it unmistakably reads as smoke.
evidence: metrics: idle/play effHue=51 effSat=0.12 -> near-neutral grey reads as smoke; faint warm cast (claim says grey-blue)

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. The labeled Density and Rise controls each produce a clear, sensible visible change a first-time user would understand: Density low empties the frame (smoke dissipates to near-black) and high fills it with thick smoke; Rise low keeps the plume hugging the bottom and high lifts it to fill the full vertical extent. Speed shows changed=false in the paused sweep (controls[0].changed=false), but per the caveat that is a paused-motion capture artifact, not a dead control.
evidence: control: density low->high meanLuma 7.5->63.3 (changed=true); rise low->high meanLuma 36.2->85.7 (changed=true)

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive. The three play frames visibly evolve — the swirls shift and the plume reshapes between captures — with frameDeltaMag rising 3.25 -> 3.48 -> 6.82, i.e. real per-frame motion. Control apply latency ~575-608ms is acceptable for a slider. Density and Rise sweeps both register changed=true.
evidence: metrics: play-1 frameDeltaMag=3.25, play-2 frameDeltaMag=3.48, play-3 frameDeltaMag=6.82 (visible motion)

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED: 'That looks like real billowing smoke now — soft swirling plumes, no blocky shelves, and the sliders actually do something.' The only quibble is the smoke is a warm-neutral grey rather than the grey-blue the description promises, which is a taste nit, not a flaw.

flags.note: Body reads as warm-neutral grey (effHue~51, effSat 0.12 with a faint cream cast) rather than the 'grey-blue' the claim describes. Reads unmistakably as smoke, so this is a taste/palette FLAG, not a blocker.

Speed control shows changed=false in the paused sweep (controls[0].changed=false); play-frame deltas confirm motion is live, so this is a capture artifact rather than a dead control, but a future capture should sweep speed during playback to prove it.
